_sources.usda: USDA FoodData Central, https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/ (record named in each entry), read 2026-10-27
_sources.nihOds: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets (Iron, Folate, Vitamin C, Vitamin K, Magnesium, Zinc, Potassium, Vitamin A, Calcium, Vitamin B12, Vitamin D, Vitamin E), https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/list-all/; reference intakes as listed in build_draft_batch.py (RDA for adult women)
_sources.niddk: NIDDK, Eating, Diet & Nutrition for Kidney Stones, read 2026-10-26: nuts and nut products, peanuts, rhubarb, spinach and wheat bran listed among foods to reduce for calcium oxalate stones

almond-milk.desc: Beverages, almond milk, unsweetened, shelf stable
almond-milk.how: Pour over cereal, blend into smoothies, or use in baking and coffee.
almond-milk.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
almond-milk.reviewNote: The calcium, vitamin D and vitamin E in this record come from fortification, and brands differ; an unfortified almond drink has far less calcium. Almond drinks contain little almond and little protein (0.4 g per 100 g).
almond-milk.name: Almond milk

butter.how: Spread thinly on bread, melt over vegetables, or use in cooking and baking.
butter.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
butter.reviewNote: Mostly fat (about 11.5 g and 102 kcal per tablespoon), mostly saturated. Salted butter; unsalted differs in sodium (not shown).
butter.name: Butter

cheddar.how: Slice into sandwiches, grate over vegetables, eggs and baked potatoes, or melt into sauces.
cheddar.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
cheddar.reviewNote: Sharp cheddar; mild and aged cheddars differ a little. Cheese is also high in sodium and saturated fat (not shown here).
cheddar.name: Cheddar cheese

cream-cheese.portion: 2 tablespoons, 1 oz (USDA: 1 oz = 28.35 g; 1 tbsp = 14.5 g)
cream-cheese.how: Spread on bread or bagels, stir into sauces and soups, or use in dips and baking.
cream-cheese.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
cream-cheese.reviewNote: Regular full-fat cream cheese; reduced-fat and whipped versions differ. Soft cheeses have their own safety questions in pregnancy that were not researched for this draft.
cream-cheese.name: Cream cheese

milk.desc: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D
milk.how: Drink it, pour over cereal, or use in porridge, soups, sauces and baking.
milk.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
milk.reviewNote: The catalogue entry does not say whole milk or skim; whole milk (3.25% fat) was used, and reduced-fat milks have less fat and energy but similar calcium. Raw (unpasteurised) milk is a different matter and is not covered.
milk.name: Milk

parmesan.how: Grate over pasta, soups, salads and roasted vegetables; a little adds a lot of flavour.
parmesan.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
parmesan.reviewNote: Grated parmesan as sold in shakers or tubs, which can include added ingredients and is lower in water than a wedge; a hard wedge has a slightly different composition. Very salty (sodium not shown).
parmesan.name: Parmesan

sour-cream.how: Dollop onto soups, baked potatoes, tacos and chilli, or mix into dips.
sour-cream.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
sour-cream.reviewNote: Regular full-fat sour cream; reduced-fat versions differ.
sour-cream.name: Sour cream

soy-milk.how: Drink it, use on cereal, or use in smoothies and baking; check whether the carton is fortified and unsweetened.
soy-milk.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
soy-milk.reviewNote: The USDA record is UNFORTIFIED soy milk; most shop-bought soy milk is fortified with calcium (and often vitamin D and B12), so its calcium is much higher than shown. Sweetened versions have more sugar.
soy-milk.name: Soy milk

heavy-cream.how: Whip for desserts or stir a little into soups and sauces.
heavy-cream.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
heavy-cream.reviewNote: High in fat (about 5.4 g and 51 kcal per tablespoon).
heavy-cream.name: Heavy cream
